quizzes.title: Howzat! Cricket Classics
quizzes.description: World Cup glory, legendary players and the basics of the gentleman's game.

questions.q: Which country won the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup?
questions.note: MS Dhoni sealed the final with a six at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium.

questions.q: How many players does each team have on the field in a cricket match?
questions.note: A cricket pitch is 22 yards long between the two sets of stumps.

questions.q: India won the first ever Cricket World Cup in 1975.
questions.note: False: the West Indies won in 1975; India's first title came in 1983.

questions.q: Which Indian batting legend is nicknamed the 'Master Blaster'?
questions.note: Accept 'Sachin' or 'Tendulkar'; he played 200 Test matches.

questions.q: Who captained India to victory in the 1983 Cricket World Cup?
questions.note: India beat the mighty West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.q: How many legal deliveries make up a standard over?
questions.note: Eight-ball overs were once used in Australia and New Zealand.

questions.q: A six is scored when the ball clears the boundary without bouncing.
questions.note: If the ball bounces before crossing the rope, it's a four.

questions.q: In which year did India win the first ICC T20 World Cup?
questions.note: India beat Pakistan in the final in Johannesburg.

questions.q: What is it called when a batter is out for zero on the very first ball they face?
questions.note: Out for zero on any later ball is simply called a 'duck'.

questions.q: Which Indian bowler took all 10 wickets in a Test innings against Pakistan in 1999?
questions.note: England's Jim Laker was the first to do it, in 1956.

quizzes.title: Football Fever
quizzes.description: World Cup history, famous goals and legendary clubs of the beautiful game.

questions.q: Which country hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.note: Uruguay beat neighbours Argentina 4–2 in the final in Montevideo.

questions.q: A standard football match has two halves of 45 minutes each.
questions.note: Referees add stoppage time for injuries and other delays.

questions.q: Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' goal in 1986 was scored against which team?
questions.note: Minutes later he scored the 'Goal of the Century' in the same match.

questions.q: Which Brazilian legend, known by one name, won three FIFA World Cups as a player?
questions.note: Accept 'Pele'; he won in 1958, 1962 and 1970.

questions.q: Which country won the 2014 FIFA World Cup in Brazil?
questions.note: Mario Götze scored the extra-time winner against Argentina.

questions.q: Which English club is nicknamed 'The Red Devils'?
questions.note: Manchester United's Old Trafford is nicknamed the 'Theatre of Dreams'.

questions.q: A goalkeeper may handle the ball anywhere on the pitch.
questions.note: False: keepers may only handle the ball inside their own penalty area.

questions.q: Which Indian city is home to the historic rival clubs Mohun Bagan and East Bengal?
questions.note: Their fierce rivalry is known as the Kolkata Derby.

questions.q: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar?
questions.note: They beat France on penalties after a 3–3 draw in the final.

questions.q: Which country won the European Championship, Euro 2016, held in France?
questions.note: Eder's extra-time goal beat the hosts 1–0 in the final.

quizzes.title: Olympic Glory
quizzes.description: Legendary champions, host cities and India's proudest Olympic moments.

questions.q: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
questions.note: Paris followed as host of the 1900 Games.

questions.q: Which Jamaican sprinter won the Olympic 100 m title in 2008, 2012 and 2016?
questions.note: Accept 'Bolt'; he ran 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships.

questions.q: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
questions.note: Pierre de Coubertin designed the rings in 1913.

questions.q: Neeraj Chopra won gold in the javelin throw at the Tokyo Olympics.
questions.note: It was India's first Olympic gold in athletics; the Games were held in 2021.

questions.q: How often are the Summer Olympic Games usually held?
questions.note: The Tokyo 2020 Games were the exception, held a year late in 2021.

questions.q: In which team sport did India win six Olympic golds in a row?
questions.note: India won field hockey gold at every Games from 1928 to 1956.

questions.q: Karnam Malleswari became India's first female Olympic medallist in 2000 in which sport?
questions.note: She won bronze at the Sydney Games.

questions.q: Olympic gold medals are made of solid gold.
questions.note: False: they are mostly silver, plated with at least 6 grams of gold.

questions.q: Which American swimmer won eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
questions.note: Accept 'Phelps'; he beat Mark Spitz's 1972 haul of seven golds at one Games.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics?
questions.note: It was the first Olympic Games held in South America.

quizzes.title: Aces, Birdies & Checkmates
quizzes.description: Tennis history, rules of the game and legends across courts, greens and boards.

questions.q: Who beat John McEnroe in the famous five-set Wimbledon final of 1980?
questions.note: It was Borg's fifth Wimbledon title in a row.

questions.q: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on clay courts?
questions.note: It is held at Stade Roland-Garros in Paris.

questions.q: Leander Paes won a bronze medal in men's singles tennis at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.
questions.note: It was India's first individual Olympic medal since 1952.

questions.q: Which Grand Slam tournament is played at the All England Club in London?
questions.note: Players must wear almost entirely white clothing there.

questions.q: In chess, which piece can move only diagonally?
questions.note: Each player starts with one light-squared and one dark-squared bishop.

questions.q: In golf, an 'eagle' means finishing a hole one stroke under par.
questions.note: False: one under is a birdie; an eagle is two under par.

questions.q: How many players does each team have on court in indoor volleyball?
questions.note: Beach volleyball is played in teams of two.

questions.q: Which Indian shuttler won Olympic silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020?
questions.note: Saina Nehwal had earlier won bronze at London 2012.

questions.q: Who became India's first chess grandmaster in 1988?
questions.note: Accept 'Anand' or 'Vishy'; he later became world champion.

questions.q: How many points is the black ball worth in snooker?
questions.note: A maximum 147 break means taking all 15 reds with blacks, then every colour.
